- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5), model often overpredicts downward moves; reduce forecast slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- Model frequently underestimates sharp upward spikes (especially after 1-2 negative sentiment days) — adjust forecast upward by 1-2% for such transitions.
- Model overestimates downward corrections after recent highs — apply a lagged mean reversion rule: if last 3 values are rising, cap forecast decline at 10% below recent peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overcorrect early in the forecast window — apply a “smoothed trend” correction: average last 5 values before forecasting next point.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, model often misses the reversal — increase forecast by 1-3% in the first 5 days of the new sentiment phase.
- Model underestimates true volatility in sentiment-driven periods — add 0.5–1.5% volatility buffer to forecast if sentiment variance > 0.3 over last 7 days.
